candidates.rationale: EPAS1 (HIF-2α) is the key oncogenic driver downstream of VHL loss (~80-90% of ccRCC); belzutifan, a HIF-2α inhibitor, is FDA-approved (VHL disease RCC, ORR ~49%; advanced RCC after prior therapy, ORR ~22% in LITESPARK-005 and PFS benefit over everolimus).
Biallelic inactivation by mutation, deletion or methylation occurs in ~80-90% of ccRCC, is the founding truncal event, and is the synthetic-lethal and pharmacologic basis for HIF-2α inhibition.

HIF-driven VEGF overexpression underlies the hypervascular phenotype; VEGF/VEGFR TKIs (sunitinib, pazopanib, axitinib, cabozantinib, lenvatinib) are standard of care, and an angiogenesis gene signature predicts TKI response (IMmotion150/151).
VEGFR2 is the principal receptor blocked by approved TKIs, with ORRs of ~25-30% for sunitinib monotherapy and ~55-70% for TKI plus PD-1 combinations.

PD-1 blockade (nivolumab, pembrolizumab) is backbone therapy, e.g. nivolumab+ipilimumab and pembrolizumab+axitinib/lenvatinib improve OS in first line, although PD-L1 expression is only a weak predictor of response.
mTOR is hyperactivated via PI3K/AKT/PTEN alterations and HIF translation; everolimus and temsirolimus are approved, though with modest benefit (median PFS ~4-5 months).

Second most frequently mutated gene (~40% of ccRCC); loss is associated with angiogenic signature and possible benefit from anti-VEGF and ICI therapy in some cohorts, though results are inconsistent (e.g., CheckMate 025 vs. Miao 2018).
Mutated in ~10-15% of ccRCC; loss is associated with high-grade disease, mutual exclusivity with PBRM1, and significantly worse overall survival, and may predict sensitivity to PARP/EZH2 strategies.
Mutated in ~10-15% of ccRCC; loss of H3K36me3 is associated with poor prognosis and genomic instability, and creates potential synthetic-lethal vulnerabilities (e.g., WEE1 inhibition).

HIF-induced carbonic anhydrase IX is expressed in >90% of ccRCC, is the basis for girentuximab imaging (REDECT: ~86% sensitivity, ~87% specificity) and radioimmunotherapy, and low expression has been linked to worse prognosis.
